headline: The book is sitting in a pre-Nvidia tape. Memory already paid.
lede: Monday sold the AI and memory sleeve into Nvidia’s Wednesday print. The only stories that matter for this book are that print, a >15% Nvidia server price hike driven by HBM/DRAM, CXMT–Apple chatter that hit MU and SNDK, Broadcom’s $60–80b Anthropic financing (and the CDS jump), Marvell’s Google custom-silicon win into Thursday’s print, and Tesla’s China recall plus another AI-chip engineer leaving. Everything else is noise.

items.title: Nvidia prints Wednesday after the close
items.what: Fiscal Q2 2027. Street ~US$92.1b revenue and US$2.09 EPS versus May guide of US$91b ±2%. KeyBanc keeps Buy / US$330 on the Rubin ramp. Seventh session down into the print.
items.impact: This is the week’s event for the whole book — stock and calls. A beat-and-raise with clean HBM commentary lifts NVDA, TSM, SEMI and should bounce MU/SNDK. A guide-down or margin squeeze hits every AI line at once. Do not add ahead of it.

items.title: Nvidia told customers AI servers go up >15% into 2027
items.what: Bloomberg/Reuters: Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin racks, memory now ~25% of high-end rack cost after server DRAM doubled. Hyperscalers already notified.
items.impact: Pricing power for Nvidia if demand holds (reward). Sticker shock on hyperscaler capex if they push out (risk). Memory ASP is the fundamental support under MU/SNDK/DRAM — the tape sold it on CXMT scare anyway. Treat the hike as confirmation of tightness, not a buy signal before the print.

items.title: CXMT–Apple China sourcing chatter
items.what: Monday tape: reports the US may allow Apple more China memory sourcing. MU ~−6%, SNDK ~−6.5%, DRAM ETF with them. Analysts calling it overreaction — CXMT qualification is low-volume China SKUs, YMTC still not approved.
items.impact: If it stays a China-handset footnote, this is a dip in a tight HBM cycle (reward after NVDA). If Apple actually dual-sources meaningful NAND/DRAM, SMSF memory is the wrong size. Wait for the Nvidia call to say whether server memory is still the bottleneck.

items.title: Broadcom PT trimmed; Marvell–Google win; AVGO prints 2 Sep
items.what: A top analyst cut the AVGO target after Marvell announced a custom AI chip deal with Google. AVGO 5y CDS +28bp as talks for US$60–80b (possibly US$100b with junior) Anthropic/AI-chip financing leak. Marvell prints 27 Aug; Morgan Stanley looks for beat-and-raise.
items.impact: Financing is demand for Broadcom silicon (reward) and leverage the bond market is starting to price (risk). Marvell’s Google win is real for MRVL this week; it is a share-of-wallet worry for AVGO, not a cancelled cycle. Size stays small on both until those two prints.

items.title: Tesla: China door-handle recall + AI-chip talent leak
items.what: Industry-wide China campaign: Tesla recalling ~2.98m vehicles (labels + software, from 25 Sep) over hidden emergency releases. Separate: senior AI hardware engineer Shishuang Sun left for DensityAI, another knock to the in-house chip/Terafab story. Nevada approved a larger robotaxi fleet the same session; stock still −3.8%.
items.impact: Recall is not a material P&L hit — software/labels, every OEM in the same rule. Talent leaving the AI-silicon effort is the actual risk to the Tesla-as-compute thesis. Robotaxi approval is longer-dated reward. Largest line in the book: do not add.

items.title: SpaceX + Nvidia Vera Rubin for orbit in 2027
items.what: Musk: space-optimised Vera Rubin NVL72 with Nvidia; SpaceXAI using Vera CPU on Grok. Nvidia also discussing a Perplexity stake ~US$30b and said Groq 3 LPX is in full production.
items.impact: Narrative bid for SPCX stock/calls and a TAM footnote for NVDA. Not 2026 cash. Treat as optionality, not a reason to add size.

items.title: Nvidia: Groq 3 LPX in production; Perplexity / Poolside talks
items.what: Full production on Groq 3 LPX inference. Reported talks on Perplexity (~US$30b) and a multibillion Poolside open-weight deal. Software/ecosystem, not the quarter.
items.impact: Supports the inference/agentic story into the print. Does not change Wednesday’s numbers. Secondary to guide and HBM commentary.

risks.title: Print risk is the book
risks.text: NVDA + TSLA + MU are the three largest names. A Nvidia miss or a soft data-centre guide reprices compute, memory, SEMI and the call book in one session. Stand aside until the print is digested.

risks.title: Memory dual-source
risks.text: If CXMT/YMTC in Apple becomes more than a China-SKU rumour, SMSF MU/SNDK/DRAM is the wrong weight. The 15% rack hike argues the opposite (tightness) — do not pre-trade either side.

risks.title: Broadcom financing scare
risks.text: CDS already jumped. A sloppy US$60–80b structure into 2 Sep earnings is a credit event that leaks into AVGO equity and the AI-capex complex.

risks.title: Tesla compute thesis
risks.text: Engineers leaving the in-house silicon effort matter more than the China recall. TSLA is the largest line; no add, no heroics on robotaxi headlines.

rewards.title: Tight memory, if Nvidia says so
rewards.text: A clean HBM/DRAM comment on the call plus the server price hike is the bounce setup for MU, SNDK and DRAM — after the print, on a confirmed dip, not before.

rewards.title: Rubin / inference stack
rewards.text: KeyBanc US$330, Groq 3 LPX production, Vera Rubin with SpaceX. If guide holds, NVDA and TSM catch the bid first.

rewards.title: Marvell–Google this week
rewards.text: Custom silicon win is already in the tape. Thursday’s print is the second catalyst. Small, not a chase.

rewards.title: Crypto sleeve already bid
rewards.text: IBIT/MSTR/BMNR/BSOL were green while AI was red. That is the hedge working, not a signal to rotate the core book.

stance: Sit. No adds into Wednesday. Heavy names stay heavy. Memory only after Nvidia, on a confirmed dip — not on the CXMT headline.
